I’m sorry, but I couldn’t locate the county‑level motor‑vehicle‑theft rates for Hawaii that cover both 2014 and 2020. The few sources I was able to find provide isolated figures (e.g., a 2014 rate for Maui County) but none give the full set of rates for all four counties (Honolulu, Hawaiʻi, Maui, Kauai) across that time span.

Because the necessary data to calculate “drop per 100,000 residents” isn’t available in the sources I accessed, I can’t identify which county had the biggest decline from 2014 to 2020.

If you have access to the Hawaii State Police or Hawaii Department of Transportation crime reports, the FBI Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) database, or county‑specific crime statistics, those would be the places to look. Once you have the year‑by‑year rates, you can compute the difference (2014 – 2020) for each county and determine the maximum drop.
